content: The test image shows corn kernels (seed part) with prominent white fluffy mycelium growing between them. Kernels appear yellowish/tan/slightly pinkish. Top candidates from seed category: Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Gibberella_Disease.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Very close-up corn kernels, pale/yellowish-tan colored, with abundant white fluffy/cottony mycelium growing between and around them. No pink, green, or black coloration.

**Reference comparison:**
- **Aspergillus**: Olive-green powdery mold — clearly eliminated
- **Trichoderma**: Blue-green/gray-green conidia on yellow kernels — eliminated
- **Gibberella**: Pink/red mold at ear tip — eliminated
- **Fusarium** (image 25): White-pinkish growth on bright yellow kernels; (image 64): white mycelium with black-discolored kernels — not a strong match
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: White mycelium growing between kernels; kernels appear pale/tan/rotted — best match

The white fluffy mycelium enveloping pale/tan kernels matches Diplodia's characteristic description of "white fungal mycelium growing over and between kernels." The kernel color (pale, somewhat rotted-looking) also aligns with Diplodia more than Fusarium.
